He demands to know if Harmon understands what the will document in his possession is worth, attempting to exploit what he believes is a valuable secret to extort money from them.
c64:p89: John Harmon reveals to Wegg that the document he has been extorting over is worthless—it is merely a will leaving the father's property to the Crown, not to Wegg as he believed. This disclosure comes during Wegg's blackmail attempt against Boffin and Harmon, moments before Harmon physically attacks Wegg for his insolence and explains the true contents of the Dutch bottle found in the Mounds.
c64:p90: Wegg confronts John Harmon about a will document he believes gives him power over Boffin's property. Harmon reveals the paper is worthless because it is an older will that has already been legally superseded, setting up the confrontation that will result in Wegg's violent expulsion.
c64:p91: Wegg confronts John Harmon about a will document, demanding to know its value. Harmon replies that the paper is worthless because it's a later will leaving everything to the Crown, not to Wegg.
c64:p92: John Harmon physically attacks Wegg after Wegg's attempt to blackmail him with a worthless forged will, shaking him violently by the cravat and pinning him to the corner as punishment for his scheming against the Boffins.
c64:p93: John Harmon confronts Wegg after revealing that the will Wegg has been blackmailing over is worthless. Harmon physically seizes Wegg by the cravat and pins him against a wall, delivering a passionate speech about Boffin's generosity and condemning Wegg's ingratitude and villainy. This marks the climactic moment where Wegg's scheme is fully exposed and he faces the consequences of his betrayal.
c64:p94: John Harmon physically confronts Silas Wegg after discovering that Wegg's blackmail document (a will) is worthless, gripping him by the cravat and shaking him violently against the wall while delivering an angry rebuke about Wegg's ingratitude and treachery.
c64:p95: John Harmon physically confronts Wegg after he attempts blackmail with a forged will. Harmon explains the true history of the Dutch bottle—a genuine will buried in the Mounds by Mr. Boffin—and reveals that Wegg's supposed evidence is worthless.
c64:p96: John Harmon holds Wegg by the cravat and forces him to look at a Dutch bottle while shaking him violently, explaining that this bottle contained his father's will that left everything to Mr. Boffin. Sloppy holds up the bottle so Wegg can see it as John Harmon confronts him about his scheme to extort money from Boffin.
c64:p97: John Harmon confronts Silas Wegg after revealing that a will he believed to be valuable is actually worthless. The Dutch bottle Wegg sought contained a later will that excluded Harmon and his sister, which Boffin discovered and buried in the Mound. Harmon explains that this will has since been legally produced and established, making the document in Wegg's hand worthless. Harmon physically threatens Wegg while delivering this revelation.
c64:p98: John Harmon physically confronts Wegg by grabbing his cravat and shaking him violently against a wall, delivering a harsh speech about the worthlessness of the forged will Wegg has been using to extort money from Boffin. This sentence describes Wegg's visible comprehension of Harmon's threat as he is being shaken.
c64:p99: John Harmon confronts the scheming Silas Wegg after his blackmail attempt has been exposed. Harmon reveals that he and Boffin deliberately allowed Wegg to believe he had discovered valuable evidence (the will in the Dutch bottle) in order to maximize his disappointment when the truth emerges. Harmon explains that they had been secretly monitoring Wegg's activities throughout, with Sloppy shadowing him, and that Venus had informed Boffin of Wegg's discovery. This is the first of two final speeches Harmon delivers to torment Wegg before he is physically ejected from the house.
c64:p100: John Harmon physically shakes Silas Wegg by the cravat while delivering a speech explaining that he and Mr. Boffin deliberately deceived Wegg about a valuable will hidden in the Mounds, ensuring Wegg's disappointment would be as severe as possible.
c64:p101: John Harmon confronts Silas Wegg after revealing that a will found in a Dutch bottle buried in the Mound proves Wegg's blackmail scheme is worthless. Harmon explains that he owes his entire fortune solely to Mr. Boffin's generosity and integrity, not to his father's will, and expresses his fury at Wegg's attempt to exploit and rise against the noble Boffins.
c64:p102: John Harmon has just finished violently confronting Silas Wegg, shaking him by the cravat and pinning him in a corner while explaining that the will Wegg discovered is worthless. Wegg, physically released, recovers his composure as Sloppy begins maneuvering behind him in preparation to physically remove him from the room.
c64:p103: Mr Boffin offers to compensate Wegg after his blackmail scheme has been exposed and defeated. Despite Wegg's attempts to extort money by threatening to reveal a compromising will, John Harmon has physically subdued him and revealed that the document is worthless. Boffin now magnanimously offers to pay Wegg to leave and set up elsewhere, showing his fundamental decency even toward someone who has betrayed and attempted to manipulate him.
c64:p104: John Harmon confronts Wegg with the truth about the Dutch bottle will and threatens him with violence. After shaking Wegg by the cravat and delivering his angry speech about Boffin's nobility, Harmon adds this additional threat, stipulating that Wegg must not only be dismissed but also banished from the premises entirely.
c64:p105: Wegg attempts to negotiate compensation after his blackmail scheme against Boffin has been exposed and defeated. Having been offered two pounds by Boffin, Wegg begins listing his losses—his ballad collection, gingerbread stock, street-vending business, and reputation—to justify a higher payment before he is physically removed from the house.
c64:p106: Wegg attempts to negotiate compensation from Boffin for his losses, mentioning his valuable ballad collection. John Harmon intervenes with this dismissive response, refusing to allow Wegg to be paid for his supposed possessions and cutting short his negotiations.
c64:p107: After John Harmon violently confronts Wegg about the worthless Dutch bottle will and humiliates him, Mr. Boffin offers to compensate Wegg for setting him up in another stall. Wegg responds by itemizing his losses—his ballad collection, gingerbread stock, and other possessions—attempting to extract payment through flattery and reluctant deference to Boffin's judgment.
c64:p108: John Harmon has just physically confronted Wegg, revealing that the will Wegg was blackmailing with is worthless—the genuine will leaving everything to Boffin was already discovered and legally established. Now Boffin offers Wegg compensation to leave peacefully, expressing bewilderment at Wegg's ingratitude and treachery after all Boffin has done for him.
c64:p109: Wegg is itemizing his losses and possessions to extract monetary compensation from Mr. Boffin after his blackmail scheme has failed, listing various items and relationships he claims to have sacrificed in their business arrangement.
c64:p110: Wegg is attempting to extort money from Mr. Boffin by listing all his possessions and losses—ballads, gingerbread, his street-stall business, and patronage connections—claiming compensation for his hardship during the Mounds leveling. Boffin, uncertain of a fair buyoff amount, mutters this line while considering what sum to offer Wegg to remove him from the house.
c64:p111: This chunk occurs during Wegg's final negotiation with Mr. Boffin after his scheme to extort money has been exposed and defeated. Wegg, facing dismissal, attempts to extract financial compensation by itemizing his losses—including his ballad collection, street stall business, and various goods—in a manipulative appeal to Boffin's supposed generosity. The passage exemplifies Wegg's avaricious desperation as he itemizes worthless possessions to justify demanding payment before being physically ejected from the house.
c64:p112: Wegg attempts to negotiate compensation from Boffin after his scheme to blackmail the Golden Dustman fails. As Boffin struggles to determine a fair payment amount, Wegg continues to itemize his losses—including his ballad collection, gingerbread stock, street-vending business, and the patronage he lost—in an effort to maximize his settlement before being forcibly ejected from the house.
c64:p113: Wegg is itemizing his losses and grievances to Mr. Boffin, requesting compensation for being cast off from his scheme. He lists the customers and social connections he has lost through his association with Boffin, presenting himself as a victim deserving financial recompense for his troubles.
c64:p114: Sloppy is backing toward Wegg along the wall in preparation to physically remove him from Boffin's house, as part of the scheme to expel the scheming Wegg after his blackmail attempt has been foiled.
c64:p115: Wegg attempts to negotiate compensation from Boffin after his schemes have been exposed and defeated. Having lost his blackmail leverage when the supposedly worthless will is revealed to be legally void, Wegg pathetically catalogs his losses and grievances—including the psychological toll of Boffin's deception—to extract money from the Golden Dustman before his inevitable expulsion.
c64:p116: Mr Wegg has failed in his blackmail attempt against Mr Boffin, having discovered that the will he sought to use as leverage is worthless. After being physically confronted and humiliated by John Harmon, Wegg now seeks compensation from Mr Boffin for his losses—including his ballad collection, his street stall business, and his damaged reputation. Mr Boffin, showing clemency despite Wegg's treachery, offers him money to start over elsewhere.
c64:p117: Wegg refuses Boffin's initial payment of two pounds, claiming he cannot accept such a meager sum given all his losses and suffering during the mound-leveling scheme. This refusal immediately precedes his violent expulsion from the house by Sloppy.
c64:p118: Silas Wegg attempts to blackmail Mr. Boffin with a forged will he claims to have discovered, demanding payment. John Harmon reveals the document is worthless and physically subdues Wegg. After refusing Boffin's offer of compensation, Wegg is physically ejected from the house by Sloppy and unceremoniously dumped into a scavenger's cart.
